page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration belonging to the E6 flexible compute series. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor utilizing the x86_64 microarchitecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading enabled, supplying 16 dedicated virtual CPUs. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per thread.

Hardware architecture for the instance emphasizes balanced general compute capability without integrated hardware acceleration or local solid-state drives. There are zero GPUs present on this shape, and local storage is listed as None, necessitating the use of external network-attached block volumes for persistent filesystem needs and operating system installations. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for primary network connectivity.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance positions this instance for horizontal application tiers, container orchestration nodes, mid-tier relational databases, enterprise web hosting, and standard continuous integration workloads that do not demand physical disk IOPS on-host.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This shape does not include local disk storage or specialized GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage requirements must be met using network-attached block volumes. One public IPv4 address is included by default. The resource distribution makes this configuration suitable for mid-sized relational database servers, enterprise web applications, build runners, and general back-end microservices requiring stable dedicated compute threads without relying on local NVMe arrays.
